english.title: Refuse to quit railway carriage at destination
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having paid your fare on the railway **(..SPECIFY STATION FROM AND TO..), knowingly and wilfully

(A)_[refused]_
(B)_[neglected]_

to quit the railway carriage on arriving at that point
english.legislation: Contrary to section 103 of the Railway Clauses Consolidation Act 1845.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
having paid your fare to a destination
knowingly and wilfully refused/neglected to quit carriage on arrival at such destination

english.notes:
(i) In Scotland this offence contravenes Section 96 of the Railway Clauses Consolidation Act 1845.
(ii) The refusal to quit must be intentional so that a person who simply sleeps on is not guilty of an offence. This section applies to cases where a person, out of truculence, refuses to leave a carriage on arrival at their destination station. Knowledge is an essential ingredient of the offence and must be proved by the prosecution; knowledge includes the state of mind of a person who shuts his mind to the obvious.
(iii) Railway employees are authorised under section 104 of this Act to detain any person offending under section 103.
(iv) Police officers attending an incident where such a detention has occurred may arrest if the conditions under section 25 of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984 apply otherwise the detained person must be released and reported for any offences which may have been committed.
